report.background:
The Department of Health (DOH) ensures that Electronic Medical Record (EMR) systems joining the Health Information Exchange (HIE) are interoperable. This supports the Universal Health Care Act's vision of coordinated and traceable referral across Health Care Provider Networks. Interoperability requires that different EMR systems exchange patient and referral information that every receiving system can read, understand and use without re-entry. This depends on a common data structure under the national HL7 FHIR standards, shared code systems and value sets, and the consistent use of national identifiers and registries for patients, health workers and facilities.

The Healthcare Interoperability Readiness Matrix for EMR Systems follow the validation process of registration, assessment of submitted documents, validation and issuance of certificate. They determine whether an EMR system offered by a third-party vendor or an in-house developer conforms to the applicable national FHIR Implementation Guides before it may be used in the HIE for electronic referral. The criteria check that referral data is complete and correctly coded on the shared health record, that the receiving system displays it as sent, that status updates flow back to the referring facility, and that errors and interruptions are handled safely. The results may serve as the basis for issuing a certificate of conformance for use in the HIE.

The objective of the evaluation is to identify any gaps in a system's conformance before it is deployed to health facilities. The Developer's Guide and Validator's Guide for each criterion let vendors prepare in advance, allow every system to be evaluated consistently, and help management identify which areas require correction or technical support.
report.scope: This testing criteria applies to EMR systems offered by third-party vendors or developed in-house that seek to be used in the HIE for electronic referral. It evaluates the EMR system itself, as a product, once for each version submitted. Testing covers the vendor's application and commitment, product documentation, terminology, referral submission and retrieval, error and exception handling, security, reports, and advanced interoperability features. All tests are conducted by the Regional Validation Team — the CHD ICT Unit with validators from PhilHealth and DICT, and witnessed by observers — on the DOH test environment (sandbox), using designated test facilities and fictional test data. No actual patient information is used. A new version or major release of the system, or an update to the Implementation Guides, requires re-testing. The engagement, deployment and operation of the system at an actual health facility are outside the scope of this form. The security part is conformance testing of defined controls and is not equivalent to a vulnerability assessment and penetration test (VAPT) or a full cybersecurity assessment.

criteria.title: Process flows of the eReferral module as implemented in the system, for all three: (a) referring, (b) receiving, (c) back-referral

criteria.title: User manual of the eReferral module contains all seven REQUIRED sections (all-or-nothing): (1) system overview & user roles, (2) referring workflow step-by-step, (3) receiving workflow step-by-step, (4) back-referral workflow, (5) downtime/offline behaviour, (6) troubleshooting & error messages, (7) vendor support contacts & escalation
criteria.evidence: User manual
criteria.developer_guide:
Submit the eReferral module user manual with a table of contents that covers all 7 REQUIRED sections. Include how users check the server status. Purpose: Checks the content of the manual once, at product level. All seven sections are REQUIRED. If one section is missing, the manual scores 0% (all-or-nothing).

Check the table of contents and the body of the manual for each of the 7 sections. Mark each sub-item (↳) below, so that the missing sections are listed.

sub_items.text: Server status check & downtime / offline behaviour

criteria.title: Supported FHIR interactions documented per resource (which resources are created, read, updated, searched), for example a CapabilityStatement (Connectathon Issue #3)
criteria.evidence: CapabilityStatement or equivalent document
criteria.developer_guide:
Submit a CapabilityStatement (or equivalent) that lists each FHIR resource used, with its supported interactions (POST, PUT, GET, search) and search parameters.

Purpose: Removes ambiguity about what the system actually sends and receives.
criteria.validator_guide: Check that the document lists each resource used in TS1/TS2 with its interactions (POST/PUT/GET/search).

criteria.title:
System architecture: integration of the eReferral function with the EMR, judged by how patient details reach the referral (not by how the system is built).
(a) Fully integrated = 100%: the eReferral function is part of the EMR. Or, it is a standalone system integrated with the EMR. Its only role is to do the referral, and it receives the patient details automatically.
(b) Standalone - manual encoding = 50%: the standalone system still needs a person to encode patient details manually (re-typing, copy-paste or re-upload).
criteria.evidence: System architecture diagram (high-level is sufficient) + demonstration
criteria.developer_guide:
Submit a system architecture diagram. Show the EMR, the eReferral function (built-in or a separate system) and how patient details flow from the EMR record into the referral. A high-level diagram is sufficient. The diagram does not need internal component, network or infrastructure details. The vendor MAY use any integration method (shared database, API, FHIR, HL7 v2, other interface).
Evidence options: the vendor MAY choose any one option that proves compliance.
(a) The full document / configuration.
(b) A high-level or redacted version, plus a signed attestation by an authorized officer that the control meets the referenced TB items.
(c) Independent certification or report (for example, ISO/IEC 27001, SOC 2, cloud-provider compliance report, penetration-test summary letter).
(d) A view-only presentation (screen share or on site). The Validators record it as "sighted" with the date, and do not keep a copy.
The vendor never needs to give source code, keys, credentials or internal network details. The evidence is used only for this validation, under the confidentiality undertaking of the Regional Validation Team (Instructions 4B).

Purpose: The important point is that the system reuses patient details recorded once in the EMR, without manual re-encoding. The vendor MAY build the eReferral function into the EMR or make it a separate system. This design choice gets no penalty.
criteria.validator_guide:
1. Review the architecture diagram.
2. Demonstration: register the Test Data patient in the EMR. Then start a referral.
3. Fully integrated: every patient detail already in the EMR (name, birth date, sex, PhilSys number, PhilHealth ID, address, contact number) appears in the referral. The user does not re-type, copy-paste or re-upload it. This applies to an eReferral function built into the EMR and to a separate system connected to it.
4. Standalone - manual encoding: the user has to encode one or more of these details manually.
5. Not Met: no diagram or no demonstration.

criteria.title: Product security and privacy design documented and stated against the Technical Baseline and NPC Circular 2023-06: (1) authentication & role-based access, (2) audit logging, (3) encryption in transit and at rest, (4) backup & recovery of data held only in the system (user accounts / credentials, audit trail, configuration), (5) privacy-by-design / privacy-by-default features (data minimisation, retention and secure disposal)
criteria.evidence: Security design document, or redacted summary + signed attestation, or independent certification, or view-only presentation
criteria.developer_guide:
Submit security and privacy design documentation that covers the five topics. For each topic, state the mechanism used. Confirm that it meets or exceeds the Technical Baseline (Reference Guide, Ch. 3) (TB-01 to TB-11). The vendor MAY use any product, platform or method that meets the baseline. If the system uses an equivalent control instead, attach a short justification with evidence (Instructions 4A).
Evidence options: the vendor MAY choose any one option that proves compliance.
(a) The full document / configuration.
(b) A high-level or redacted version, plus a signed attestation by an authorized officer that the control meets the referenced TB items.
(c) Independent certification or report (for example, ISO/IEC 27001, SOC 2, cloud-provider compliance report, penetration-test summary letter).
(d) A view-only presentation (screen share or on site). The Validators record it as "sighted" with the date, and do not keep a copy.
The vendor never needs to give source code, keys, credentials or internal network details. The evidence is used only for this validation, under the confidentiality undertaking of the Regional Validation Team (Instructions 4B).

Purpose: Describes the security features of the system in measurable terms. The Shared Health Record keeps the exchanged referral data. The backup covers data that exists only in the system. Topic 5 also gives facilities (the personal information controllers) the information for their own Privacy Impact Assessment (NPC Circular 2023-06 §5 and §7).
criteria.validator_guide:
Count the five topics. A topic is Met if both conditions are true:
1. Any accepted evidence option shows compliance (full or redacted document with signed attestation, independent certification, or view-only presentation recorded as sighted).
2. The topic maps to the referenced TB items (or the Technical Lead accepted an equivalent control).
Record the evidence option used in Notes. Level 2D tests that the controls work.
Mark each sub-item (↳) below. The tool counts Achieved automatically.

sub_items.text: Encryption in transit and at rest, password storage (TB-01 to TB-04)
Backup & recovery of data held only in the system: user accounts / credentials, audit trail, configuration (TB-09)
Privacy-by-design / privacy-by-default: data minimisation, retention and secure disposal (TB-11, NPC Circular 2023-06 §7–9 and §28–30)

criteria.title: Version/change management: release notes for the version under test and a committed timeline for updating to new IG versions
criteria.evidence: Release notes + update commitment
criteria.developer_guide:
Submit release notes for the version under test. Also submit a written timeline for adopting new PH Core / PHeReF IG versions.

Purpose: The vendor will apply updates to the draft IGs in a controlled, traceable way.
criteria.validator_guide:
Check the release notes for the version under test.
Check the written update timeline.

sheets.title: Level 2A — TS0 Terminology & Registry Validation (GATE)
sheets.intro: Before the EMR submits (TS1) or reads (TS2) an eReferral, every coded element MUST use the official terminology. Every registry value or patient identifier MUST follow the official registry. The Terminology & Registry Sources (Reference Guide, Ch. 4) name the exact server, registry or API for each concept (SRC-01 to SRC-15). The critical items MUST score 100%. They are the IG-required bindings (TS0-01, TS0-02) and invalid-code handling (TS0-03). They also include PSGC and NHFR (★ in TS0-06) and the PhilHealth / PhilSys identifiers (TS0-07). TS1, TS2 and Level 3 cannot work without them. Other items (display text, code-system validity, NHWR, DSWD) have normal weight but are not critical. The vendor MAY choose how to get the values (live look-up, scheduled sync or cached copy). Test this part first.
sheets.note: Count criteria: mark each sub-item (rows marked ↳). The tool calculates Required, Achieved, Result and Outstanding automatically.

criteria.title: PH Core coded elements: values match the official PH Core / base FHIR value sets (required bindings, not locally invented)
criteria.evidence: Screenshot of each dropdown + server response ($expand / $validate-code)
criteria.developer_guide:
Use the PH Core / base FHIR value sets for each coded field listed (sex, contact point). The source is SRC-05. Use the source named in the Terminology & Registry Sources (Reference Guide, Ch. 4). For coded values, this source is the DOH HIE terminology server. The vendor MAY choose runtime look-up, scheduled sync or cached copy.

Purpose: These bindings are REQUIRED in the IG. A wrong code makes the whole referral fail validation (TS1-T.02). Thus this criterion is critical.
criteria.validator_guide:
1. Check that the configured terminology endpoint of the system is the DOH HIE terminology server (Terminology & Registry Sources, Reference Guide, Ch. 4).
2. Open each field / dropdown listed as a sub-item.
3. Compare the options with the value set on the server ($expand), or check the submitted code ($validate-code).
4. A sub-item is Met only if every option / submitted code belongs to the bound value set.
Mark each sub-item (↳) below. The tool counts Achieved automatically. ★ = critical sub-item. If a ★ sub-item is Not Met (or N/A), the criterion counts as a critical failure.

sub_items.text: Civil status: MaritalStatus value set (required binding in ERefPatient)
Accompanied by / next of kin relationship: RelatedPerson relationship type (required binding on Patient.contact.relationship)

criteria.title: PHeReF coded elements: values match the official PHeReF value sets (not locally invented)
criteria.evidence: Screenshot of each dropdown + server response ($expand / $validate-code)
criteria.developer_guide:
Use the PHeReF value sets for each coded field. The sources are SRC-01 to SRC-04 and SRC-09. Use the source named in the Terminology & Registry Sources (Reference Guide, Ch. 4). For coded values, this source is the DOH HIE terminology server. The vendor MAY choose runtime look-up, scheduled sync or cached copy.
Referral Category → ServiceRequest.category (Referral Category VS, SNOMED CT: 73770003 Emergency / 440655000 Outpatient, required binding).
Priority → ServiceRequest.priority (EReferralPriority: routine / urgent / stat, required binding).
Reason for Referral → ServiceRequest.reasonCode (Reason for Referral (Service Type) VS, SNOMED CT).
Practitioner Role → PractitionerRole.code (Practitioner Role VS, required binding).
Task status → Task.status (FHIR TaskStatus: requested, received, accepted, rejected, completed).

Purpose: TS1, TS2 and the Level 3 reports cannot work if these codes are wrong. All five are critical.
criteria.validator_guide:
1. Check that the configured terminology endpoint of the system is the DOH HIE terminology server (Terminology & Registry Sources, Reference Guide, Ch. 4).
2. Open each field / dropdown listed as a sub-item.
3. Compare the options with the value set on the server ($expand), or check the submitted code ($validate-code).
4. A sub-item is Met only if every option / submitted code belongs to the bound value set.
Mark each sub-item (↳) below. The tool counts Achieved automatically. ★ = critical sub-item. If a ★ sub-item is Not Met (or N/A), the criterion counts as a critical failure.

sub_items.text: Practitioner Role: PHeReF Practitioner Role VS (required binding)
Referral Category: PHeReF Referral Category VS, SNOMED CT Emergency / Outpatient (required binding)
Priority: EReferralPriority, routine / urgent / stat (required binding)
Reason for Referral (service type): PHeReF Reason for Referral VS, SNOMED CT
Task status: FHIR TaskStatus (requested / received / accepted / rejected / completed)

criteria.title: Invalid codes are handled gracefully: the system prevents a code outside the bound value set, or it clearly shows the SHR's rejection to the user and lets the user correct and resend (Connectathon Issue #25)
criteria.evidence: Screenshot of the block / error message + server-side evidence of the rejected and corrected submission
criteria.developer_guide:
Use approach (a) or approach (b). The vendor MAY choose the approach.
(a) Validate coded fields before saving / sending (for example, pick-lists built from the value set, $validate-code). Then a user cannot enter an out-of-value-set code.
(b) When the SHR rejects the referral, show the user a clear error that names the field. Let the user correct the referral and resend it.

Purpose: Wrong codes never silently enter the referral or the dashboards. Users never have a failed referral that they cannot see.
criteria.validator_guide:
The Validator (server-side) tries to submit one code outside the value set (for example, for Reason for Referral).
Met if the EMR blocks / flags the code before sending.
Also Met if the EMR shows the SHR's rejection in understandable terms, and the user can correct and resend successfully.
Not Met if the EMR does not show the error to the user, or if the code is accepted.

criteria.title: Codes are shown with their official display text (no locally renamed labels)
criteria.evidence: Screenshots side-by-side
criteria.developer_guide:
Show the official display text from the terminology server. Do not rename code labels locally. The EMR MAY show a local translation in addition to the official text, but not instead of it.

Purpose: Everyone sees the same meaning for the same code.
criteria.validator_guide:
Compare the labels that the EMR shows for 3 value sets with the terminology server display. Count the value sets that match.
Mark each sub-item (↳) below. The tool counts Achieved automatically. ★ = critical sub-item. If a ★ sub-item is Not Met (or N/A), the criterion counts as a critical failure.

sub_items.text: Reason for Referral: official display text

criteria.title: Codes from international code systems (where the PH Core / PHeReF IG binds them) are valid on the DOH terminology server: SNOMED CT, LOINC and ICD-10
criteria.evidence: $validate-code / $validate output
criteria.developer_guide:
The IG binds some fields to SNOMED CT (practitioner role, referral category, reason for referral), LOINC (vital-sign Observation codes) or ICD-10 (working impression, where bound). For these fields, send codes that exist in the edition loaded on the DOH terminology server. Use the correct system URI.

Purpose: Codes are valid and comparable across facilities.
criteria.validator_guide:
The Validator (server-side) checks every SNOMED CT, LOINC and ICD-10 code in the Test Data referral. The check uses CodeSystem/$validate-code on the DOH terminology server (or $validate on the submitted bundle). A sub-item is Met only if every code of that system is valid.
Mark each sub-item (↳) below. The tool counts Achieved automatically. ★ = critical sub-item. If a ★ sub-item is Not Met (or N/A), the criterion counts as a critical failure.

sub_items.text: SNOMED CT: codes valid, system = http://snomed.info/sct
LOINC: vital-sign codes valid, system = http://loinc.org
ICD-10: working-impression codes valid, system = http://hl7.org/fhir/sid/icd-10 (N/A if not bound)

criteria.title: Geographic, facility and health-worker values come from the official national registries and match them: PSGC, NHFR, NHWR
criteria.evidence: Screenshot of each field + registry / server response
criteria.developer_guide:
Take PSGC codes from the PSA PSGC release that the DOH announced (SRC-10). Take facility codes from the NHFR (SRC-11). Take practitioner identifiers from the NHWR / PRC (SRC-12). The vendor MAY choose how to access the registry (API, scheduled sync or official download). The release MUST match the DOH server.

Purpose: PSGC and NHFR are critical. The receiving facility finds its referrals by NHFR code (TS2-01). The Level 3 reports group by facility and municipality.
criteria.validator_guide:
1. Open each field listed as a sub-item.
2. Compare the values with the source named in the Terminology & Registry Sources (Reference Guide, Ch. 4).
3. Server-side check: confirm that the submitted codes exist in that registry / the DOH terminology server.
4. For NHFR (TS0-06.2): try to type a facility that is not in the NHFR. The system MUST allow the user to select only NHFR facilities (absorbs Rev 6 L4-09).
Mark each sub-item (↳) below. The tool counts Achieved automatically. ★ = critical sub-item. If a ★ sub-item is Not Met (or N/A), the criterion counts as a critical failure.

sub_items.text: PSGC code: Philippine Standard Geographic Code (PSA)
NHFR code: National Health Facility Registry. Facilities are selected only from the NHFR, not free-typed (absorbs Rev 6 L4-09)
NHWR: health worker identifier / licence no. (National Health Workforce Registry)

criteria.title: Patient identifiers (PhilHealth ID and PhilSys number) are captured, validated and sent with the official PH Core identifier system, so that every patient record is linked to them (critical)
criteria.evidence: SHR Patient resource + error screenshot for the malformed value
criteria.developer_guide:
For every patient:
(1) Provide fields for the PhilHealth ID and the PhilSys number.
(2) Validate the format per the PH Core IG. Reject malformed values.
(3) Send each identifier as Patient.identifier with the PH Core identifier system (PHCorePhilHealthID / PHCorePhilSysID).
(4) Use a verification service where one is made available for the sandbox. Examples: the PhilSys Verifier through the DSWD dxCLOUD API under an agreement with DSWD (SRC-14), or a PhilHealth service (SRC-13).

sheets.title: Level 2D — Security, Reliability & Exception Handling
sheets.intro: Baseline technical safeguards that are REQUIRED before live patient data is exchanged. Each criterion states the outcome tested. The Technical Baseline (Reference Guide, Ch. 3) (TB-01 to TB-14) gives the minimum measurable specification. The vendor MAY use any product, platform or method that meets or exceeds the baseline. The Validator tests outcomes by using the system (black-box). Where documents are necessary, vendors MAY choose any evidence option in Instructions 4B. Vendors never need to give internals or trade secrets. Disclaimer: this is security conformance testing of defined controls. Passing it is not equivalent to passing a vulnerability assessment and penetration test (VAPT) or a full cybersecurity assessment. (TEC-14 only checks that an independent assessment exists.) Exception handling (TS3-01 to TS3-09): the EMR MUST NOT show a failed exchange as successful. The EMR MUST explain the error and allow correction. The EMR MUST leave exactly one correct referral on the SHR. Test Data Section D (TD-D##) gives the inputs and expected results.
sheets.note: Count criteria: mark each sub-item (rows marked ↳). The tool calculates Required, Achieved, Result and Outstanding automatically.

criteria.title: All data exchange is encrypted in transit and meets Technical Baseline TB-01 and TB-02 (TLS 1.2 or higher, strong cipher suites, valid certificate)
criteria.evidence: Endpoint list + TLS scan report per endpoint
criteria.developer_guide:
Encrypt every endpoint that the eReferral uses (EMR ↔ SHR, terminology server, user access) with TLS 1.2 or higher and a valid certificate. Disable plain HTTP or redirect it to HTTPS. Disable SSL, TLS 1.0/1.1 and weak cipher suites (TB-01, TB-02). The vendor MAY use any web server, gateway, proxy or cloud service.

Purpose: Patient data cannot be read or changed while it moves over the network.
criteria.validator_guide:
1. List every endpoint that the system uses.
2. Validator (server-side) scans each endpoint with a TLS testing tool (for example, testssl.sh, nmap ssl-enum-ciphers or an online TLS checker).
3. Met only if every endpoint meets all four conditions:
(a) it uses https://.
(b) it negotiates TLS 1.2 or 1.3 only.
(c) it offers no cipher suite that TB-02 lists as not acceptable.
(d) it has a valid, unexpired certificate that matches the host name.

criteria.title: Each user has a unique account (no shared logins)

Require one account per user. Do not use generic or shared accounts. Protect accounts as TB-05 specifies (minimum password length, lock-out or throttling after failed attempts, no default passwords). The vendor MAY use any identity method (local accounts, LDAP / Active Directory, single sign-on, OpenID Connect).

Purpose: Every action can be traced to a person.
criteria.validator_guide: Check that the system requires a unique account for each user. Check that no generic or shared accounts are used for test referrals. Then try (a) a password shorter than the TB-05 minimum and (b) repeated failed log-ins. Met only if all three behave as TB-05 requires.

criteria.title: Backup and restore of data held only in the system (user accounts / credentials, roles, audit trail, configuration)
criteria.evidence: Restore demonstration, or restore-test record, or provider backup report + signed attestation
criteria.developer_guide:
Provide backup and restore for the data that only the system holds: user accounts / credentials, roles, audit trail and configuration. Use a backup that meets TB-09 (automated, encrypted, stored separately). The vendor MAY choose the backup tool and location.
Evidence options (the vendor MAY choose any one that proves compliance):
(a) the full document / configuration.
(b) a high-level or redacted version, plus a signed attestation by an authorized officer that the control meets the referenced TB items.
(c) independent certification or report (for example, ISO/IEC 27001, SOC 2, cloud-provider compliance report, penetration-test summary letter).
(d) a view-only presentation (screen share or on site). The Validators record it as "sighted" with the date and do not keep a copy.
Source code, keys, credentials and internal network details are never necessary as evidence. Evidence is used only for this validation, under the Regional Validation Team's confidentiality undertaking (Instructions 4B).

Purpose: Data that exists only in the system (not on the Shared Health Record) can be recovered after a failure.
criteria.validator_guide:
System-only data includes user accounts, audit trail and configuration. Met if any one option below shows a restorable TB-09 backup of system-only data:
(a) a live restore demonstration in the test environment.
(b) a dated restore-test record (log or report) that the Technical Lead accepts.
(c) a hosting / cloud-provider backup report, plus a signed vendor attestation that the backup includes system-only data and that restores are tested.
Record the evidence option used in Notes.

criteria.title: Data held by the system is encrypted at rest (TB-03) and user passwords are stored only as salted adaptive hashes (TB-04)
criteria.evidence: Any accepted evidence option (view-only demo, masked screenshots, certification + signed attestation)
criteria.developer_guide:
Encrypt personal and health data that the system holds (database, stored files/attachments and backups) with AES-128 or stronger. Keep the keys separate from the data (TB-03). Store passwords only as salted hashes that use Argon2id, bcrypt, scrypt or PBKDF2 (TB-04). The vendor MAY use any encryption layer (full-disk/volume, database, file or field level).
Evidence options (the vendor MAY choose any one that proves compliance):
(a) the full document / configuration.
(b) a high-level or redacted version, plus a signed attestation by an authorized officer that the control meets the referenced TB items.
(c) independent certification or report (for example, ISO/IEC 27001, SOC 2, cloud-provider compliance report, penetration-test summary letter).
(d) a view-only presentation (screen share or on site). The Validators record it as "sighted" with the date and do not keep a copy.
Source code, keys, credentials and internal network details are never necessary as evidence. Evidence is used only for this validation, under the Regional Validation Team's confidentiality undertaking (Instructions 4B).

Purpose: A stolen disk, database copy or backup does not expose patient data or passwords.
criteria.validator_guide:
Met if any accepted evidence option shows compliance with both TB-03 and TB-04. Examples of accepted options:
(a) a view-only demonstration of the encryption setting and of the stored form of one test password.
(b) configuration screenshots with key values masked.
(c) a cloud-provider encryption setting or independent certification that covers encryption at rest, plus a signed attestation that names the password-hashing algorithm.
Not Met if any evidence shows plain-text, reversible or MD5 / SHA-1 password storage, or no encryption at rest. Record the evidence option used in Notes.

criteria.title: Access boundaries hold: failed log-ins are handled safely, users cannot see or act on another facility's referrals, and users cannot raise their own privileges
criteria.evidence: Screenshots / HTTP responses per step (black-box)
criteria.developer_guide:
Enforce authorisation on the server side for every screen and API call. Enforce it by role (TEC-03) and by facility (a user acts only for the facility or facilities assigned to that user). Reject guessed or changed record IDs that belong to another facility. Use generic log-in error messages, and lock-out / throttling as TB-05 specifies.

Purpose: This prevents the most common real-world breaches: staff or outsiders who read records that they are not entitled to read.
criteria.validator_guide:
Use two test accounts and TD-D18 to TD-D21. User A is a referring clinician at Facility A. User B is a receiving clinician at Facility B.
1. Enter a wrong password for a valid user and for a non-existent user. Check that the two messages are identical. Check that the account is locked or throttled after the TB-05 limit.
2. As User A, try to open a referral that is addressed only to Facility C (list, search, direct link).
3. Change the referral ID or patient ID in the URL or API call to an ID that belongs to Facility C.
4. As a non-administrator, open an administrator page by direct URL / API. Then try to change your own role.
5. Call the EMR's API without a valid session / token.
Mark each sub-item (↳) below. The tool counts Achieved automatically. ★ = critical sub-item. If a ★ sub-item is Not Met (or N/A), the criterion counts as a critical failure.

sub_items.text: Failed log-in: generic message (no user enumeration) and lock-out / throttling as TB-05 specifies (TD-D18)
Cross-facility access blocked: referrals of another facility cannot be listed, searched or opened (TD-D19)
Direct object reference blocked: a changed ID in the URL / API does not show the data of another facility (TD-D20)
No privilege escalation: admin functions cannot be reached by direct URL / API, and users cannot change their own role (TD-D21)
Requests without a valid session / token are refused (HTTP 401 / 403 or redirect to log-in)

criteria.title: Sessions and accounts end when they should: log-out invalidates the session, expired sessions / tokens are refused, and revoked accounts lose access
criteria.evidence: Screenshots / HTTP responses + time of each step
criteria.developer_guide:
Invalidate the session on the server at log-out. Refuse expired sessions and tokens. When an administrator deactivates an account, block new log-ins immediately. Also end the active sessions of that account within the TB-12 limit.

Purpose: Former staff and stolen sessions cannot continue to access patient data.
criteria.validator_guide:
1. Log in, copy the session (or note the page) and log out. Then press Back / replay the request. Check that access is refused.
2. Wait past the idle / token expiry (TB-06 / TB-12) and repeat an action. Check that the system asks for re-authentication.
3. An administrator deactivates a logged-in test user. Check that the user cannot log in again. Check that the open session ends within the TB-12 limit.
Mark each sub-item (↳) below. The tool counts Achieved automatically.

sub_items.text: Session invalid after log-out (Back / replayed request refused)
Expired session / token refused, and the system asks for re-authentication
Deactivated account: new log-in blocked immediately, and active session ended within the TB-12 limit

criteria.title: Error messages, client-side code and logs do not expose secrets, system internals or patient data beyond what the user has permission to see
criteria.evidence: Screenshots + log sample or signed attestation
criteria.developer_guide:
Show users generic error messages (no stack traces, SQL, file paths or server versions). Keep credentials, tokens and API keys out of browser / mobile code, URLs and browser storage (TB-07). Keep full identifiers and clinical content out of application logs, except where the TB-08 audit requires them (TB-13).

Purpose: Error screens and logs are a frequent source of data leaks.
criteria.validator_guide:
1. Trigger errors (TD-D03, a non-existent page, a broken request) and read the messages.
2. Open the browser developer tools (or inspect the mobile app traffic). Look for secrets in the source, URLs and local / session storage.
3. Review a sample application log from the test session, or accept a signed attestation with a redacted sample (Instructions 4B).
Mark each sub-item (↳) below. The tool counts Achieved automatically.

sub_items.text: Error messages show no stack trace, SQL, paths, versions or unauthorised patient data
No credentials / tokens / API keys in client code, URLs or browser storage
Application logs exclude secrets and unnecessary personal data (TB-13)

criteria.title: The audit log cannot be changed through the application and records security events
criteria.evidence: Audit log extract + screenshots
criteria.developer_guide:
Make audit entries append-only for every application role, including administrators. Log failed log-ins, role / permission changes and account deactivation. Restrict audit log viewing / export to an authorised role (TB-08).

Purpose: An audit trail that can be edited proves nothing.
criteria.validator_guide:
1. As an ordinary user and as an administrator, try to edit or delete an audit entry through the application.
2. Check that the log shows the failed log-ins (TEC-09.1), the role change attempt (TEC-09.4) and the deactivation (TEC-10.3).
3. Try to open the audit log with a non-authorised role.
Mark each sub-item (↳) below. The tool counts Achieved automatically.

sub_items.text: Audit entries cannot be edited or deleted through the application (any role)
Role / permission changes and account deactivation are logged
Audit log viewing / export restricted to an authorised role

criteria.title: Outgoing connections verify server certificates, and any API the EMR exposes is protected against abuse
criteria.evidence: Connection error screenshot / log + throttling response or documented control
criteria.developer_guide:
Verify the certificate of the SHR / terminology server on every connection (no 'trust all certificates' setting). If the EMR exposes its own API to the internet, apply rate limiting or equivalent abuse controls.

Purpose: This prevents interception (man-in-the-middle) and denial-of-service by request flooding.
criteria.validator_guide:
1. TD-D22: the DOH provides a sandbox endpoint with an invalid / expired / untrusted certificate. Configure the EMR to connect to it. Met if the EMR refuses to connect. If the DOH did not provision the endpoint, mark N/A with the reason.
2. If the EMR exposes an internet-facing API, send repeated requests (within the agreed test limit). Confirm throttling or a documented control. N/A if the EMR exposes no API.
Mark each sub-item (↳) below. The tool counts Achieved automatically.

sub_items.text: Connection refused to an endpoint with an invalid / untrusted certificate (TD-D22)
Rate limiting / abuse control on any internet-facing API that the EMR exposes (N/A if none)

criteria.title: An independent vulnerability assessment (VAPT or authenticated scan) of the version under test exists, with no unresolved critical / high findings
criteria.evidence: VAPT / scan executive summary + signed attestation (or full report, view-only)
criteria.developer_guide:
Provide evidence of a security assessment of the version under test (or the same major version). The assessment is a vulnerability assessment and penetration test, or an authenticated vulnerability scan. An independent party or a separate security team did it within the last 12 months (TB-14). Critical / high findings are fixed or covered by a remediation plan that the Technical Lead accepts. Evidence options are as Instructions 4B specifies (for example, executive summary + signed attestation).

Purpose: Black-box conformance testing cannot replace a security assessment. This criterion checks that one was done.
criteria.validator_guide: Check the date, the scope (product + version), the independence of the assessor and the status of critical / high findings. Met only if all four are acceptable. This criterion does not make this validation a security assessment (see the disclaimer above).

criteria.title: A referral without an element that the IG makes mandatory is not shown as sent, the reason is shown to the user, and the corrected referral is accepted
criteria.evidence: Screenshot of the block / error + server-side evidence of the rejected and the accepted submission
criteria.developer_guide:
This applies to a referral that lacks an element with minimum cardinality ≥ 1 in the PHeReF / PH Core profiles. These elements are in FHIR Traceability (Reference Guide, Ch. 5), column 'Cardinality'. For such a referral, prevent sending, or handle the SHR rejection (HTTP 4xx with OperationOutcome). Show the user which item is missing. Keep the referral as not sent, and allow correction and resend.

Purpose: A referral that the SHR refused MUST NOT look 'sent' to the referring clinician.
criteria.validator_guide:
1. Use TD-D01 (patient birth date left blank) and TD-D02 (receiving facility not selected).
2. For each sub-item, try to submit. Met if either of these occurs:
(a) the EMR blocks it before sending, with a clear message.
(b) the SHR rejects it, and the EMR shows the rejection in understandable terms and keeps the referral as not sent.
3. Correct the value and resend. On the SHR, check that exactly one accepted referral exists.
Mark each sub-item (↳) below. The tool counts Achieved automatically. ★ = critical sub-item. If a ★ sub-item is Not Met (or N/A), the criterion counts as a critical failure.
Server-side evidence is any one of these items:
(a) The Interoperability Layer transaction log (for example, OpenHIM).
(b) An Inferno / official FHIR validator report.
(c) The raw FHIR request / response payload that the developer provides and that is captured during the session.

sub_items.text: Missing Patient.birthDate (1..1): blocked or rejection shown, and referral not marked sent (TD-D01)
Missing receiving facility (ServiceRequest.performer): blocked or rejection shown (TD-D02)
After correction, the referral is accepted and exactly one ServiceRequest / Task exists on the SHR

criteria.title: Malformed values (wrong data type or format) are prevented, or the SHR rejection is handled without data loss
criteria.evidence: Screenshots + server-side evidence (where submitted)
criteria.developer_guide:
Validate data types and formats before sending, or handle the SHR rejection clearly. Examples of formats: dates in ISO 8601, numeric vital signs with UCUM units, identifier formats as PH Core specifies. The EMR MUST NOT lose entered data when an error occurs.

Purpose: Bad formats are caught early and do not reach other facilities.
criteria.validator_guide:
1. Use TD-D03 (impossible date, for example 2026-02-30), TD-D04 (non-numeric heart rate) and TD-D05 (birth date in the future).
2. Met per sub-item if both conditions are true:
(a) the system blocks the value, or shows the SHR rejection clearly.
(b) the system keeps the rest of the entered referral for correction.
Mark each sub-item (↳) below. The tool counts Achieved automatically.
Server-side evidence is any one of these items:
(a) The Interoperability Layer transaction log (for example, OpenHIM).
(b) An Inferno / official FHIR validator report.
(c) The raw FHIR request / response payload that the developer provides and that is captured during the session.

sub_items.text: Impossible date (TD-D03): prevented or rejection handled
Non-numeric vital-sign value (TD-D04): prevented or rejection handled
Birth date in the future (TD-D05): prevented or rejection handled

criteria.title: References to a facility, practitioner or patient that does not exist are prevented, or the rejection is handled
criteria.evidence: Screenshots + server-side evidence
criteria.developer_guide:
Resolve every reference before sending, or handle clearly the SHR rejection of a reference that cannot be resolved. Resolve facilities from the NHFR (TS0-06) and practitioners from the registered list.

Purpose: A referral cannot be addressed to a facility that does not exist.
criteria.validator_guide:
1. Use TD-D06 (NHFR code not in the registry) and TD-D07 (practitioner not registered in the sandbox).
2. Met per sub-item if the system blocks it, or shows the SHR rejection clearly and keeps the referral as not sent.
Mark each sub-item (↳) below. The tool counts Achieved automatically.
Server-side evidence is any one of these items:
(a) The Interoperability Layer transaction log (for example, OpenHIM).
(b) An Inferno / official FHIR validator report.
(c) The raw FHIR request / response payload that the developer provides and that is captured during the session.

sub_items.text: Unknown receiving facility NHFR code (TD-D06): prevented or handled
Unregistered practitioner as requester (TD-D07): prevented or handled

criteria.title: Submitting the same referral twice (double click, resend after timeout, re-opened draft) leaves only one referral on the SHR
criteria.evidence: SHR search result (count of ServiceRequest / Task) + server-side evidence
criteria.developer_guide:
Make sending idempotent. Examples:
(a) disable the Send action while waiting.
(b) give each referral a business identifier, and use conditional create (If-None-Exist) or a transaction Bundle with conditional entries.
(c) check the SHR before resending.
The vendor MAY choose the method.

Purpose: Duplicate referrals distort Level 3 counts and make the receiving facility prepare twice.
criteria.validator_guide:
1. TD-D08: click Send twice quickly.
2. TD-D09: after a send, use the resend / retry function of the system for the same referral.
3. Validator (server-side) searches the SHR (ServiceRequest by patient and authored date, or by business identifier).
Met per sub-item only if exactly one ServiceRequest and one Task exist for that referral.
Mark each sub-item (↳) below. The tool counts Achieved automatically. ★ = critical sub-item. If a ★ sub-item is Not Met (or N/A), the criterion counts as a critical failure.
Server-side evidence is any one of these items:
(a) The Interoperability Layer transaction log (for example, OpenHIM).
(b) An Inferno / official FHIR validator report.
(c) The raw FHIR request / response payload that the developer provides and that is captured during the session.

sub_items.text: Double Send (TD-D08): exactly one ServiceRequest and one Task on the SHR
Resend / retry of an already accepted referral (TD-D09): no second referral created

criteria.title: Connection loss during or before sending: no data is lost, the referral is sent (automatically or by documented fallback) after recovery, and exactly one copy arrives
criteria.evidence: Screenshots + server-side evidence + fallback record (if manual)
criteria.developer_guide:
Queue referrals made during connection loss and resend them automatically, or provide a documented manual fallback (user manual L1-02.5). After recovery, the referral MUST arrive once, with the original date/time referred (absorbs Rev 6 TEC-06).

Purpose: Referrals continue during outages without loss or duplication.
criteria.validator_guide:
1. TD-D10: disconnect the network. Create and send a referral. Then reconnect.
2. TD-D11: interrupt the connection while a send is in progress (for example, disable the network adapter immediately after Send).
3. Met per sub-item if both conditions are true after recovery:
(a) exactly one copy is on the SHR with the original authoredOn.
(b) the user was told the status (queued / failed / sent).
Mark each sub-item (↳) below. The tool counts Achieved automatically. ★ = critical sub-item. If a ★ sub-item is Not Met (or N/A), the criterion counts as a critical failure.
Server-side evidence is any one of these items:
(a) The Interoperability Layer transaction log (for example, OpenHIM).
(b) An Inferno / official FHIR validator report.
(c) The raw FHIR request / response payload that the developer provides and that is captured during the session.

sub_items.text: Offline creation (TD-D10): queued or documented fallback followed, and user sees status
Interruption mid-send (TD-D11): no loss, and exactly one copy after recovery
Original date/time referred kept after delayed sending (ServiceRequest.authoredOn)

criteria.title: If one part of the referral fails, no half-saved referral is left on the SHR and the EMR does not report success
criteria.evidence: Server-side evidence of the failed attempt + SHR search showing no orphan resources
criteria.developer_guide:
Send the referral so that it succeeds or fails as a whole. Examples: a FHIR transaction Bundle (all-or-nothing) as in the IG example (ExampleERefSubmissionBundle), or compensating clean-up when resources are sent one by one. Report failure to the user.

Purpose: A ServiceRequest without its Task, Patient or clinical data is unusable for the receiving facility.
criteria.validator_guide:
1. TD-D12: include one invalid resource in the referral (for example, an Observation with a code outside LOINC, prepared with the developer).
2. Submit. Validator (server-side) checks the SHR.
Met per sub-item if no ServiceRequest / Task / partial resources from that attempt remain, and the EMR shows the failure.
Mark each sub-item (↳) below. The tool counts Achieved automatically. ★ = critical sub-item. If a ★ sub-item is Not Met (or N/A), the criterion counts as a critical failure.
Server-side evidence is any one of these items:
(a) The Interoperability Layer transaction log (for example, OpenHIM).
(b) An Inferno / official FHIR validator report.
(c) The raw FHIR request / response payload that the developer provides and that is captured during the session.

sub_items.text: No orphan or half-saved resources from the failed attempt on the SHR
EMR does not show the referral as sent, and the user can correct and resend

criteria.title: When the terminology server or a registry (NHFR / PSGC) is unavailable, the EMR degrades gracefully and never sends invented codes
criteria.evidence: Screenshots + server-side evidence of codes sent
criteria.developer_guide:
When a look-up service is unreachable, use a validated cached copy, or block the coded field with a clear message. The cached copy comes from a scheduled sync (see Terminology & Registry Sources, Reference Guide Ch. 4). Never substitute free text or locally invented codes for a bound element.

Purpose: An outage of a national service MUST NOT corrupt the exchanged data.
criteria.validator_guide:
1. TD-D13: the DOH makes the terminology server unreachable for the test account (or the developer configures the EMR to use a dead endpoint).
2. TD-D14: do the same for the NHFR / facility list.
3. Met per sub-item if both conditions are true:
(a) the EMR uses a valid cached value set, or blocks with a clear message.
(b) any code sent is valid (TS0 check on the SHR).
Mark each sub-item (↳) below. The tool counts Achieved automatically.
Server-side evidence is any one of these items:
(a) The Interoperability Layer transaction log (for example, OpenHIM).
(b) An Inferno / official FHIR validator report.
(c) The raw FHIR request / response payload that the developer provides and that is captured during the session.

sub_items.text: Terminology server unavailable (TD-D13): cached valid codes or clear block, and no invented codes
Facility registry unavailable (TD-D14): cached NHFR list or clear block, and no free-typed facility

criteria.title: A rejected or expired system credential (EMR ↔ SHR) is reported clearly, nothing is silently dropped, and no secret appears in the message
criteria.evidence: Screenshot of the message + server-side evidence (401 / 403, then success after restore)
criteria.developer_guide:
Detect HTTP 401 / 403 from the SHR. Tell the user (or administrator) that the connection credential failed. Keep the referral as not sent / queued. Never show tokens, passwords or keys in messages or logs (TB-07, TB-13).

Purpose: Expired credentials are a common cause of silent referral loss.
criteria.validator_guide:
TD-D15: the DOH revokes or expires the system credential of the test EMR (or the developer configures an invalid one). Send a referral.
Met only if all these conditions are true:
(a) the user sees an understandable failure.
(b) the referral stays not sent / queued.
(c) the referral is sent after the credential is restored.
(d) no secret is shown.
Server-side evidence is any one of these items:
(a) The Interoperability Layer transaction log (for example, OpenHIM).
(b) An Inferno / official FHIR validator report.
(c) The raw FHIR request / response payload that the developer provides and that is captured during the session.

criteria.title: Receiving side: retrieval during an SHR outage is handled, nothing is missed after recovery, and the same referral is never listed twice
criteria.evidence: Screenshots of incoming list + server-side evidence
criteria.developer_guide:
When the SHR is unreachable, show the user that the incoming list can be out of date. After recovery, retrieve every referral addressed to the facility. If the same notification or resource arrives twice, show the referral once (match by resource ID / business identifier).

Purpose: No incoming referral is lost or duplicated at the receiving facility.
criteria.validator_guide:
1. TD-D16: make the SHR unreachable from the receiving EMR. Submit two referrals from the referring side. Then restore the connection.
2. TD-D17: re-deliver / re-read the same referral (for example, replay the notification or force a second poll).
Met per sub-item as described.
Mark each sub-item (↳) below. The tool counts Achieved automatically.
Server-side evidence is any one of these items:
(a) The Interoperability Layer transaction log (for example, OpenHIM).
(b) An Inferno / official FHIR validator report.
(c) The raw FHIR request / response payload that the developer provides and that is captured during the session.

sub_items.text: Outage shown to the user (list marked out of date / connection error)
After recovery, both referrals appear without manual ID entry (TD-D16)
Duplicate delivery (TD-D17): referral listed once only

sheets.title: Level 3 — Report Generation & Dashboard

criteria.title: Printable referral form contains all TS1 data elements (DOH referral form), checked by form section
criteria.evidence: Printed form (scanned)
criteria.developer_guide:
Provide a printable referral form that includes all TS1 data elements. The vendor MAY choose the layout and section order.

Purpose: A paper copy can go with the patient if needed.
criteria.validator_guide:
Print the Test Data referral. Compare each form section with the Test Data sheet. A section is Met only if every field in it is printed correctly. Write any missing field in Notes.
Mark each sub-item (↳) below. The tool counts Achieved automatically.

sub_items.text: Facility details: referring and receiving facility names, NHFR codes, addresses, HCPN (TS1-01, TS1-02)
Patient details: name, PhilSys, PhilHealth, birth date / age, sex, civil status, address, contact, PWD, accompanying person (TS1-04, TS1-05)

Referral status: current status and receiving facility response (TS1-12, TS2-11)

criteria.title: Referral linelist contains: (1) patient, (2) referring facility, (3) facility type, (4) facility classification, (5) TAT, (6) filter by month/year
criteria.evidence: Linelist screenshot/export
criteria.developer_guide:
Provide a referral linelist with the 6 columns / filters listed below.

criteria.validator_guide:
Count the columns / filters below that are present.
Mark each sub-item (↳) below. The tool counts Achieved automatically.

criteria.title: Linelist total equals the number of test referrals (Test Data Section B)
criteria.evidence: Linelist export + Test Data match
criteria.developer_guide:
Ensure the linelist shows every referral exactly once (no loss, no duplicates).

criteria.title: Counts of Incoming / Outgoing / Received referrals match the expected values
criteria.evidence: Report screenshot + Test Data
criteria.developer_guide:
Count incoming, outgoing and received referrals from the referral (Task) status.

Enter the system values in Test Data column C. Count the 3 values that show MATCH.

criteria.title: Counts of Deferred / Denied and Redirected referrals match

criteria.developer_guide:
Count deferred / denied and redirected referrals.

criteria.validator_guide:
Count the 2 values that show MATCH in Test Data.
Mark each sub-item (↳) below. The tool counts Achieved automatically.

criteria.title: Top reasons for referral are counted and ranked correctly

Count and rank referrals by reason for referral.

Count the 4 reason values that show MATCH in Test Data.

criteria.title: Government / Private facility counts (incoming and outgoing) match

criteria.developer_guide:
Count referrals by service capability of the receiving facility (RHU to Level 3).

criteria.validator_guide:
Count the 5 capability values that show MATCH in Test Data.

criteria.title: Average turnaround time (TAT = date/time received − date/time referred) matches the expected value (±1 minute)

Compute turnaround time from the recorded date/time referred and date/time received.

criteria.validator_guide:
Compare the system value with the Expected TAT in Test Data. Met if MATCH.

criteria.title: Linelist reconciles with the aggregate counts (same totals in both) (from DOH draft)
criteria.evidence: Both reports

Make the linelist and aggregate reports use the same data and filters.

criteria.evidence: Dashboard screenshots

Restrict dashboard viewers to de-identified, aggregated data, with no names or IDs in views or exports.

criteria.title: New referral appears on the receiving facility's list without manual refresh (time limit deferred, for information)
criteria.evidence: Screen recording (OPTIONAL)

Refresh incoming referral lists automatically, without manual refresh. The vendor MAY choose polling, push or IOL notification. A time limit will be set after the consultant's recommendation.

criteria.evidence: Screen recording / screenshots

Show an alert / pop-up for each new incoming referral.

Count and rank referrals by working impression / diagnosis (ICD-10 coded) for the selected period.

criteria.evidence: Report screenshots + Test Data Section C
criteria.developer_guide:
Assign each referral to a period by the date/time referred (ServiceRequest.authoredOn) in Philippine Standard Time. IND-01 defines this rule.

Retrieve the Section C referrals C1–C6 that the DOH pre-loaded on the SHR with fixed timestamps (Test Data Section C). sheets.title: Level 4 — Advanced Interoperability
sheets.intro: Advanced interoperability. Rev 7 separates two tracks. Core-track items are fundamental interoperability requirements. They will migrate to Level 2 (minimum conformance) as soon as the PHeReF IG models them. (IG v0.1.0 does not yet model back-referral and the multi-tier referral chain.) Maturity items are capability targets that stay OPTIONAL. Moved to Level 2 in Rev 7: status timestamps (L4-06 → TS2-13), patient de-duplication (L4-08 → TS1-16) and NHFR-sourced facility data (L4-09 → TS0-06.2). The Section column shows the track.

criteria.title: Receiving facility sends a back-referral that arrives at the original referring facility
criteria.evidence: Screenshots at both EMRs + SHR resource ID
criteria.developer_guide:
Implement back-referral as the PHeReF IG specifies. Send it to the SHR and address it to the original referring facility.

Purpose: This closes the care loop: the patient's home facility knows what happened.
criteria.validator_guide: Complete the Test Data referral and send a back-referral. Met if it appears at the referring EMR and on the SHR.

criteria.title: Back-referral contains: (1) final diagnosis/outcome, (2) treatment given, (3) follow-up instructions/recommendations
criteria.evidence: Screenshot
criteria.developer_guide:
Include final diagnosis/outcome, treatment given and follow-up instructions in the back-referral.

Purpose: The home facility has what it needs to continue care.
criteria.validator_guide:
Count the 3 elements that are present and correct at the referring EMR.
Mark each sub-item (↳) below. The tool counts Achieved automatically.

criteria.title: Referral form is pre-filled from data already in the patient's EMR record (no re-typing)
criteria.evidence: Screen recording
criteria.developer_guide:
Pre-fill the referral form from data that is already in the patient's record (demographics, vitals, diagnosis), so that the user does not enter it again.

Purpose: This was the main gap found at the Connectathon: users re-keyed data instead of reusing it.
criteria.validator_guide:
Register the test patient with demographics, vitals and diagnosis first. Open a new referral. Count the 10 fields listed in the Notes that are pre-filled correctly.
Mark each sub-item (↳) below. The tool counts Achieved automatically.

criteria.title: Receiving facility can import the received referral data into its EMR record without re-typing
criteria.evidence: Screen recording
criteria.developer_guide:
Let the receiving facility import the retrieved referral data into its patient record without re-typing.

Purpose: True interoperability at the receiving side.
criteria.validator_guide:
Count the same 10 fields that are imported automatically into the receiving patient record.
Mark each sub-item (↳) below. The tool counts Achieved automatically.

criteria.title: Attachments (for example, laboratory result PDF) sent with the referral can be opened at the receiving facility (Connectathon Issue #23)
criteria.evidence: Screenshot of opened file
criteria.developer_guide:
Store and retrieve attachments (for example, laboratory result PDF) so that they open at the receiving facility.

Purpose: Lab results travel with the patient.
criteria.validator_guide: Attach the Test Data lab file (TS1-09). Met if it opens correctly at the receiving EMR.

criteria.title: Multi-tier referral: primary → district → apex preserves the chain (each step linked to the previous)
criteria.evidence: SHR resources for each step
criteria.developer_guide:
Link each onward referral to the previous one as the IG defines.

Purpose: Supports real escalation of care.
criteria.validator_guide: Do a 3-step referral chain. Met if the SHR shows each referral linked to the previous one.

criteria.title: Referral can be cancelled/revoked by the referring facility, and the receiving facility sees the cancellation (Connectathon Issue #19)
criteria.evidence: Screenshots at both EMRs
criteria.developer_guide:
Support cancel / revoke of a referral, and send the status to the receiving facility (if the IG version supports it).

Purpose: This prevents facilities from preparing for patients who are not coming.
criteria.validator_guide: Cancel one test referral. Met if the receiving EMR shows it as cancelled. If the tested IG version does not support it yet, mark N/A with the reason.
